newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-O'BRIEN'S GRAND SLAM LEADS BLUE JAYS PAST TIGERS. [CORRECTED 19:04 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-O'BRIEN'S GRAND SLAM LEADS BLUE JAYS PAST TIGERS. [CORRECTED 19:04 GMT]

text.p: Charlie O'Brien blasted a grand slam in the eighth inning and had six runs batted in for the Toronto Blue Jays to give Pat Hentgen his fourth straight victory, a 7-2 win over the Detroit Tigers on Wednesday. (Corrects to make clear O'Brien hit just one home run in the game.)
Hentgen (4-1) allowed two unearned runs in the first inning and not much else. He struck out eight and walked one in his second complete game of the season.
In his last three starts -- all wins -- the 1996 American League Cy Young Award winner has an ERA of 0.00, allowing three unearned runs in 26 innings.
Batterymate O'Brien broke up a 2-2 game with his first career grand slam, a blast to left off reliever Mike Myers.
"Six RBI? That's not my strength," O'Brien said. "My job's to call the game. There were some good (hitting) situations for me today."
The Blue Jays bounced back from a shutout loss and won for the ninth time in 12 games.
In Kansas City, Jose Offerman and Jay Bell each knocked in two runs in the seventh inning as the Kansas City Royals handed the Boston Red Sox their sixth straight loss, 6-2.
Chili Davis had two hits, including a homer, and Offerman and Tom Goodwin each had two hits for Kansas City, which has won six of its last nine games and improved to 4-0 against Boston this season.

At Minnesota, Paul O'Neill doubled in the tying run with two outs in the ninth inning and drilled an opposite-field homer in the 12th to rally the New York Yankees to their fourth straight win, a 6-5 victory over the Minnesota Twins.
The Yankees have won seven of their last eight games and handed the Twins their 17th loss in 21 games.
"I'm looking for the ball and I'm praying to hit it hard somewhere," O'Neill said. "You hit a ball in the gap here and you get a double. This one got up and carried out of here."
The Yankees have out-homered the opposition 25-3 in the last 14 games and are 18-6 in their last 24. The Twins have lost their 18th of 23 games.
At Texas, Billy Ripken's sacrifice fly with one out in the bottom of the 10th inning scored Will Clark and lifted the Texas Rangers to a 4-3 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
Juan Gonzalez had three hits and two RBI for the Rangers.
John Wetteland (2-0) allowed one hit and struck out three over two scoreless innings as the Rangers won for the fifth time in six games.

In Oakland, Jose Canseco and Matt Stairs each homered twice and Ariel Prieto allowed two runs over 6-1/3 innings as the Oakland Athletics ended their season-high seven-game losing streak with a 7-4 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.
Prieto allowed six hits and struck out five without a walk.
Cal Eldred was ripped for six runs and nine hits over six innings for the Brewers.

In Anaheim, reliever Dennis Springer allowed two hits over 5 2/3 scoreless innings and Darin Erstad, Garret Anderson and Jim Edmonds hit two-run homers as the Anaheim Angels rallied from a five-run deficit for a 6-5 victory over the Baltimore Orioles.
Springer, a knuckleball specialist, replaced ineffective starter Shigetoshi Hasegawa to begin the fourth.

Springer struck out six and walked one before he was relieved by left-hander Mike Holtz with two outs in the ninth. Holtz gave up an infield single to Brady Anderson before striking out Roberto Alomar for his first major-league save.

In Seattle, Brent Gates' three-run homer keyed a five-run fourth inning and Ken Griffey Jr. added his major-league leading 17th home run as the Seattle Mariners held off the Chicago White Sox 9-7 in the opener of a two-game series.

Jamie Moyer (3-0) won his third game in as many decisions since missing more than a month with a strained left forearm. He allowed three runs and nine hits over six innings, walking one and striking out three.
